pool.text: Following the Norman Conquest, Southampton became the major port of transit.
The first mayor of Southampton served, marking 800 years of the office.
The Franciscan friary in Southampton was founded around this period.
Ringleaders of the Southampton Plot were tried for high treason.
The port served as departure point for the Pilgrim Fathers aboard Mayflower.
A Parliamentary garrison moved into Southampton during the English Civil War.
Lucia Foster Welch was elected as the first female mayor.
Southampton Art Gallery opened to hold national and international quality exhibitions.
Heavy bombing destroyed the Woolston factory and killed local civilians.
The operation of the tram system in Southampton came to an end.
University College at Highfield was upgraded to the University of Southampton.
The town of Southampton acquired official city status.
Southampton Container Terminals first opened and continued to expand.
A monorail system was proposed for Southampton.
Cross-channel car ferries stopped operating from Southampton except for Isle of Wight services.
Southampton City Council took over most functions to become a unitary authority.
Westquay Shopping Centre opened as the city's largest retail centre.
17 Port and Maritime Regiment received recognition in Southampton.
Station studios in the Northam area closed down.
Southampton City Council estimated port contributions to air pollution.
